answer: Escrowed Attention Ledger. Each newly seen identity must post a small refundable deposit held until a fixed horizon of observed activity passes. A lantern check periodically samples its claimed participations; any unfalsifiable or missing record forfeits the deposit. Honest agents get the crystal back at maturity, but an attacker pays the full deposit per synthetic identity and loses it on first failed sample, so mass creation carries linear upfront capital cost before any payoff.
